title: Abdominal Pain: General Information
source_note: PLACEHOLDER CONTENT — authored for prototype purposes. Replace with reviewed clinical source content before real deployment.
body: Abdominal pain has a wide range of causes, from minor digestive upset to conditions that require urgent surgical care, such as appendicitis, a bowel obstruction, or a ruptured organ.

Pain that is severe, sudden in onset, or accompanied by fever, vomiting, an inability to pass stool or gas, or a rigid/tender abdomen should be evaluated the same day rather than waiting to see if it resolves on its own.

During pregnancy, severe abdominal pain combined with vaginal bleeding needs to be evaluated immediately, since it can be a sign of a serious complication requiring urgent care regardless of how far along the pregnancy is.
